title: Mastering Peripheral Ulcerative Keratitis (PUK)
summary: An essential guide to the diagnosis, systematic workup, and multimodal management of PUK. Designed for residents, this review covers classic presentations, systemic associations, and surgical considerations.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation: The Slit Lamp Exam
sections.content: Slit lamp anterior segment photo showing peripheral thinning and ulceration extending from 1 to 5 o'clock with limbal injection and scleral thinning. The scleral hue is visible, while the rest of the cornea remains clear. No KPs are present. The AC appears formed; however, assessment of depth via focal slit beam is mandatory. Patient is phakic; lids show MGD. This picture is consistent with Peripheral Ulcerative Keratitis (PUK).

rows: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), SLE, Wegener’s (GPA), Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN), Relapsing polychondritis, Crohn disease
Mooren’s ulcer, Terrien’s marginal degeneration, Marginal keratitis, Pellucid marginal degeneration, Acne rosacea, Exposure/Neurotrophic keratopathy, Trauma

sections.title: Systemic Red Flags
content: Recurrent nasal bleeding (Wegener's/GPA)
Joint pain/swelling (RA)
Hand deformities (Boutonniere, Swan neck, Ulnar deviation)
Malar rash (SLE)
Rhinophyma/Telangiectasia (Rosacea)
Generalized weakness

sections.title: Management Framework
content: Step 1: Multidisciplinary approach with Rheumatology for systemic immunosuppression.
Step 2: Control acute disease with systemic steroids (often pulsed IV).
Step 3: Long-term control using immunosuppressive agents and biological blockers.
Step 4: Supportive care: Preservative-free lubricants and prophylactic topical antibiotics.
Step 5: Anticollagenase therapy with oral Tetracycline (Doxycycline 100mg BID).
Step 6: Surgical intervention (e.g., conjunctival excision or tectonic grafting) for perforation or medical failure.

sections.title: Clinical Investigation Workup
content: Ocular: Corneal scrapings for culture/sensitivity.
Blood Work: CBC, BUN, Creatinine, Urinalysis, ESR.
Infectious Screening: VDRL, FTA-ABS, PPD/Mantoux, Chest X-ray.
Immunology: ANA, dsDNA, C-ANCA, Rheumatoid Factor (RF).

content.explanation: Diagnostic of Wegener's. Management: Systemic Cyclophosphamide + Steroids. Resistant cases: Ciclosporin, Azathioprine, or Plasmapheresis. Topical: Cyclosporine, Acetylcysteine, and aggressive epithelial protection.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Topical steroids are generally avoided in PUK as they may worsen corneal thinning.
Relapsing polychondritis may be an exception where topical steroids are considered.
Always perform a Seidel test to rule out occult perforation.
Assess corneal sensation and lid function to exclude neurotrophic or exposure components.
Doxycycline is indicated in nearly all PUK cases for its inhibitory effect on matrix metalloproteinases (anticollagenase effect).
